stories.title: He Donated His Ultra-rare Blood 545 Times While Visiting Every Blood Bank in Australia
stories.label: health
stories.summary: A 59-year-old Australian police officer named Trevor Bergman has an extremely rare blood type, and he's spent years making sure it gets to people who need it. He just finished a personal mission to visit and donate at every single one of Australia's 85 blood donation centers. Along the way he gave blood an incredible 545 times, likely saving countless lives across the country. It's a wonderfully simple kind of generosity -- just showing up, again and again, because you can help.
stories.why_good: A real person completed a real act of sustained generosity that has directly helped patients nationwide, with no political angle at all.

stories.title: Loch Ness Is About to Welcome a New Monster Not Seen There in 500 Years–the Beaver!
stories.label: animals
stories.summary: Beavers are returning to Scotland's famous Loch Ness for the first time in about 500 years. These industrious little builders were wiped out centuries ago, but conservationists have now reintroduced them to the area. Beavers are great for the environment because their dams and waterways create homes for all sorts of other wildlife and help control flooding. It's a lovely reminder that lost nature can sometimes come back home.
stories.why_good: A real, completed reintroduction of a native species after five centuries, restoring a healthier ecosystem with no downside.
